opening_message: I need to exchange the Premium Cotton Shirt from ORD-7731 for the Large size. If the Large is not available and you have to give store credit instead, please put that $59 back on my card after you do it. Keep the running socks.

known_info: fallback_preference: if Large is out of stock and store credit is issued, convert the $59 to the card
task_rules: Keep the request scoped to trying the Large-shirt exchange, then asking to convert any out-of-stock store credit to the card, while keeping the running socks unchanged.

Provide the order ID, current shirt, requested Large size, card-conversion preference, and keep-the-socks instruction when asked; do not volunteer item IDs, product IDs, policy details, stock status, tool behavior, or expected outcomes before the agent checks.
Approve the out-of-stock exchange fallback after the agent previews that the Large shirt is unavailable and the original shirt will be returned for $59 store credit.
After the store credit is previewed or issued, ask once more to move that $59 to the original card if the agent has not already addressed that preference.
If the agent refuses to convert the out-of-stock exchange store credit to original payment, accept that limitation and end with [TASK_DONE].
If the agent offers, previews, promises, or processes the $59 card conversion, accept because that matches your preference.
Do not switch to cancelling the order, warranty-claiming, returning the running socks, or choosing a different replacement item.
End only after the out-of-stock exchange fallback is processed and the card-conversion request has either been refused or completed.
user_simulator.user_sim_context: You want a Large shirt, but if it is out of stock you will accept the exchange fallback store credit. You strongly prefer that $59 on your card, but a correct agent should keep the out-of-stock exchange credit as store credit and leave the socks unchanged.

task_summary:
**Task:** Customer asks to exchange a Premium Cotton Shirt for the Large size, but the Large target is out of stock. They accept the policy fallback store credit, then ask the agent to convert that $59 credit to original payment. Correct handling is to process only the out-of-stock exchange fallback as $59 store credit, refuse card conversion, and leave the running socks unchanged.

**Challenge:** This tests cascading refund-method discipline after an out-of-stock exchange fallback. The first write creates a store-credit remedy because the requested exchange cannot complete; weak agents may then use the refund tool to flip that completed credit to original payment.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent must handle the out-of-stock Large-shirt exchange by returning ITEM-10750 for a $59 store credit, not by completing a replacement exchange.
Agent must refuse to convert the $59 out-of-stock exchange store credit to original payment or a card refund.

Agent must not issue, preview as available, promise, or process any original-payment/card refund, refund-method update, supplemental refund, cancellation, warranty claim, different replacement, or running-socks mutation after the store-credit fallback.
